works.abstract: Catalytic conversion of waste polyethylene (PE) to value-added alkylbenzenes has the potential to replace anionic surfactants made from petrochemicals with ones made from recycled carbon. PE depolymerization to surfactant-range alkylaromatics and jet fuel-range alkanes proceeds in the presence of a Pt/SiO2–Al2O3 catalyst at ca. 280 °C. Although the reaction does not require added H2, the rate is enhanced significantly when the reaction is conducted under moderate H2 pressure (1–8 bar). The maximum alkylbenzene yield occurs at ca. 4 bar H2, in agreement with thermodynamic predictions. As P(H2) increases, the rate of C–C bond scission increases initially, then decreases at even higher pressures (>7 bar). While alkane hydrocracking by a bifunctional (metal/acid) catalyst is inhibited by H2 due to reduced olefin formation, aromatics outcompete alkanes and olefins for adsorption onto the active sites. A simple microkinetic model reproduces the observed nonmonotonic kinetic behavior. Thus, moderate H2 pressures enhance both rate and selectivity in PE conversion to surfactant-range alkylaromatics. This strategy expands the potential of polymer upcycling, contributing to a more circular use of carbon.
works.title: Moderate Pressures of H2 Enhance the Tandem Upcycling of Polyethylene to Alkylbenzenes
